question: A train passes a station platform in 60 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 40 seconds. If the speed of the train is 63 km/hr, calculate the length of the platform.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = 63 km/hr = 17.5 m/s

Train length = 17.5 × 40 = 700 m

Platform + train = 17.5 × 60 = 1050 m

Platform length = 1050 − 700 = 350 m

**∴ Answer = 350 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to cross man = 40 sec

Time to cross platform = 60 sec

Speed = 63 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert speed ⇒ 63 × 5/18 = 17.5 m/s

⇒ Length of train = 17.5 × 40 = 700 m

⇒ Train + platform = 17.5 × 60 = 1050 m

⇒ Platform length = 1050 − 700 = 350 m

**∴ The correct answer is 350 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Train Concept

Crossing a man ⇒ distance = train length

Platform Case

Distance = train length + platform length

Conversion

km/hr to m/s ⇒ multiply by 5/18
